findings.title: Snapshot exhaustion rejects otherwise valid fonts
findings.message: Every footprint load now consumes one of only 32 global snapshot slots, including fonts with no deferred tables. Successful snapshots are released only by finalizers. A scan can therefore exhaust the slots before garbage collection runs and reject ordinary fonts; retaining 32 fonts with deferred readers prevents further admission indefinitely. This introduces font-loading failures on normal installations with more than 32 fonts.
findings.suggestion: Release snapshots deterministically when no deferred reader retains them, and provide an eager-loading fallback when snapshot admission is exhausted rather than failing the font load. Use explicit ownership or reference counting for snapshots retained by deferred readers.

findings.title: Footprint loading copies every font in full
findings.message: The unconditional snapshot in footprint loading copies the entire source font to temporary storage before parsing, even when it has no sbix table or cannot use deferred parsing. Scanning a font directory now reads and writes every font in full, including large tables that footprint extraction would otherwise skip. This can substantially increase scan latency and temporary-disk traffic.
findings.suggestion: Inspect the table directory before creating a snapshot and preserve the existing direct-reader path for fonts that do not need deferred resources. For eligible fonts, consider snapshotting only the deferred table bytes rather than the entire file.
